rows.note: This is the all-purpose term for rubble, especially a pile left after a building collapses or is demolished.

example.english: After the building collapsed, the whole site was covered in rubble.
example.traditional: 棟大廈冧咗之後，成個地盤都係瓦礫。
example.jyutping: dung3 daai6 haa6 lam3 zo2 zi1 hau6 seng4 go3 dei6 pun4 dou1 hai6 ngaa5 lik1

rows.note: Use this when the rubble specifically consists mainly of broken stones rather than bricks or tiles.

example.english: This mountain path is covered in rubble, so it is very slippery.
example.traditional: 呢條山路鋪滿碎石，行落去好跣。
example.jyutping: ne1 tiu4 saan1 lou6 pou1 mun5 seoi3 sek6 haang4 lok6 heoi3 hou2 sin2

rows.note: Use this when the rubble specifically consists of broken bricks and roof tiles.

example.english: After the demolition, the doorway was piled high with rubble, so nobody could get through.
example.traditional: 拆屋之後，門口堆滿碎磚瓦，行都行唔過。
example.jyutping: caak3 uk1 zi1 hau6 mun4 hau2 deoi1 mun5 seoi3 zyun1 ngaa5 haang4 dou1 haang4 m4 gwo3
